_comment: Known defects on current code, per profile. A fault or invariant
listed here is expected to fail; the run reports it as XFAIL and
stays green. Once it passes - for a fault, on every one of its
injections - the run reports XPASS and FAILS, so the entry is
removed and the issue closed. Some passes among failures only
mean a timing-dependent defect was missed that time, and are
reported without failing the run. Every entry names the issue
that tracks the defect. Optional max_recovery_seconds and
max_stall_seconds override the default bounds for a fault.
For faults the expectation covers the stall during the window only;
failing to recover after the window, or a harness error injecting
the fault, always fails the run.
Profiles differ in window length, so a defect that trips the stall
bound in a 60s window (pr, nightly) may not in a 20s one (smoke).

client_handshake_then_hang.issue: https://github.com/lfreleng-actions/sigul-docker-k8s/issues/12 - patch 11 sheds a silent mid-request peer after 120 s; the bound is that plus slack
https://github.com/lfreleng-actions/sigul-docker-k8s/issues/12 - patch 11 sheds a silent mid-request peer after 120 s; the bound is that plus slack

client_stop_mid_sign.issue: https://github.com/lfreleng-actions/sigul-docker-k8s/issues/12 - patch 11 sheds a silent mid-request peer after 120 s; the bound is that plus slack

net_bandwidth_squeeze.issue: https://github.com/lfreleng-actions/sigul-docker-k8s/issues/31 - a slow but steady client holds the bridge's only slot; intermittent, since it needs a large upload in flight when the squeeze starts

sigul-bridge: no sustained RSS growth.issue: https://github.com/lfreleng-actions/sigul-docker-k8s/issues/32 - grows about 19 MB/h under sustained load with flat process and descriptor counts

sigul-server: no sustained RSS growth.issue: https://github.com/lfreleng-actions/sigul-docker-k8s/issues/32 - grows about 7-13 MB/h under sustained load with flat process and descriptor counts

proc_wedge_bridge.issue: https://github.com/lfreleng-actions/sigul-docker-k8s/issues/33 - every bridge health check tests a live process or a listening socket, both of which a wedged daemon keeps, so it is never replaced

proc_wedge_server.issue: https://github.com/lfreleng-actions/sigul-docker-k8s/issues/33 - liveness only fails once the bridge sheds the wedged server's connections, measured at about 324 s against a 180 s bound
